plan: Economic theory suggests bidding exactly at my private value of $9 is the dominant strategy. This means I should bid $9.0 to maximize my expected profit. By bidding my true value, I ensure I only win when the prize is worth more to me than the second-highest bid. This strategy minimizes the risk of overpaying and provides the most rational approach given the single-round nature of this auction.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $20. This means bidding truthfully eliminates the risk of strategic under or overbidding. Since values are independently drawn each round, there's no historical information to adjust my strategy. By bidding $20, I maximize my potential profit - if I win, I'll earn the difference between my value and the second-highest bid, and if I lose, I lose nothing.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly at my private value ($20) is the dominant strategy in a second-price sealed bid auction. This eliminates the risk of overbidding and ensures I maximize potential profit. Since values are independently drawn and this is a single round, strategic complexity is reduced. I'll bid precisely at my true value, which prevents potential losses from bidding too high or missing out by bidding too low.
